findings.passage: The coin flip holds the question this profile follows.
findings.problem: The title promises a man who 'keeps leaving the bigger number', but the opening story shows him taking the bigger number: the article itself says YouTube 'offered me more money than twitch' and fewer required hours. A newcomer comes out of the hook unsure what the coin flip is an example of. Is it walking away from size, or (as the text later shows) wanting to be wanted? The article never says what number, if any, the Twitch exit cost him. The first real case of leaving the bigger route (the MrBeast month) doesn't arrive until the fifth H2.
findings.acceptance_test: By the end of the four intro paragraphs, a reader with no prior knowledge can say in one sentence what the coin flip shows and name a documented choice where he gave up the bigger route. Either the hook spells out that link, or the title/persona promise is matched to what the hook actually shows. No unsourced claim is added that the YouTube move cost him audience.

findings.passage: When a high-school friend's wedding clashed with his Valorant team's playoff in 2023, he said "interpersonal relationships is the real value in life" and called his mom.
findings.problem: This reverses the source's context. In S02 (HealthyGamerGG, about 01:30:36 to 01:32:39), his inner 'guy' says 'you gotta rep the team'. The relationships line is his guilty pushback against that answer. His mom then reassures him 'in his answer' ('decisions been made'), and he says the guy 'was right but it felt bad'. The friend is someone he had spoken to only a handful of times in eight years. As written, an unfamiliar reader will assume he picked people over the team. The next sentences then use the moment as part of a 'provider streak'.
findings.acceptance_test: The passage either states the outcome as the transcript gives it (the relationships line was the doubt; he went with the team-side answer and his mom told him the decision was made) or drops the example. Nothing in the 'fits neither' paragraph or the Eight-wing sentence relies on it as evidence that he puts relationships first.

findings.passage: A man who says he drinks only socially because of his family history hosted a party where drinking was the format.
findings.problem: The rule the article quotes is 'I only drink if other people are drinking.' A drinking-themed party with others drinking does not break that rule, so the 'contradiction' an attentive newcomer is told to sit with falls apart against the article's own quote. Because it touches his disclosed family alcoholism and the Mang0 enabling criticism, this reads as an implied hypocrisy charge the record doesn't support.
findings.acceptance_test: Any remaining tension is stated so the quoted rule doesn't refute it (for example: he names a genetic risk and still built a show around drinking). Otherwise the sentence is cut. A reader comparing it with the earlier quote finds no mismatch, and the family disclosure is still used only as the reason for his rule.

findings.passage: The cleanest test is a choice he made and then unmade.
findings.problem: Four passages each crown a different piece of evidence as decisive: 'That is the strongest evidence for Type 3 in the record', 'This is the Three's best moment in the record', 'This passage separates the two types best' (the trophy), and 'The cleanest test is...' (the MrBeast month). Add the recurring 'Both readings can hold those lines' and 'Most single moments here fit both', and the middle of the article becomes a running score. A newcomer can't tell which evidence actually decides the call, and the momentum turns into back-and-forth instead of building.
findings.acceptance_test: Exactly one passage is named as the main discriminator, and it matches the summary under 'The case for Type 3'. Every other section closes on something new about Ludwig rather than a superlative or a 'both types fit' verdict, and no two passages claim to be the best or cleanest test.

findings.passage: At his own wedding, watching his best friend walk out, the first place his mind went was the end.
findings.problem: The final image is strong, but (a) the evidence record never calls Slime his best friend; S05 and S16 only name him, and the earlier mention says 'his friend Slime'. (b) It arrives under 'What the record cannot show', right after a paragraph about missing testimony, with nothing tying 'endings' to the question the intro set up. A newcomer can't tell whether it is evidence, a counterpoint, or a coda.
findings.acceptance_test: Slime's relationship to Ludwig is either sourced in the evidence record or described as the sources describe it, and he is identified clearly the first time he appears. The ending either sits under a heading that fits it or follows one hedged sentence linking endings to the profile's open question (or to 'away from limits, boredom and pain'). That sentence must not claim the thought proves a type.

findings.passage: Since leaving Twitch he has built a game show, a chessboxing championship, a creative agency, and Tip To Tip trips without phones or maps across Japan in 2025 and China in 2026.
findings.problem: Orientation gaps pile up for a reader who doesn't know streaming. 'Mogul Mail' is cited from the first paragraph but never identified as his own channel, and Mogul Mail, Mogul Money and Mogul Moves blur together. 'Tip To Tip' is never explained. The Iced Coffee Hour is unexplained. 'Mario Kart World event' reads like a typo to someone who doesn't know the game. The income 'number' that went from 30,000 to 15,000 has no unit. 'The provider streak suggests to some an Eight wing' uses wing jargon nobody defines and a vague 'to some'. The reader also never learns what he is known for now or how big he is.
findings.acceptance_test: On first mention, a newcomer can tell what each of these is: Mogul Mail, Mogul Money, Mogul Moves, Tip To Tip and The Iced Coffee Hour. The 30,000 figure gets a unit only if the source supports one; otherwise it stays 'a number that tracked his income'. The Eight-wing line either explains what a wing is in plain words and who suggests it, or is cut. One sourced sentence gives his current scale or best-known formats.

findings.passage: YouTube's final offer "allowed me to stream way less hours a month," which "gives me more time to do cool … that I'm super excited about."
findings.problem: The ellipsis removes a noun (an expletive), so the quoted sentence doesn't parse. 'they … should want me', 'you're the … best' and 'really … sweaty' read fine, but 'do cool … that' stops a newcomer cold.
findings.acceptance_test: Each elided quotation still reads as a grammatical sentence: end the quote before the elision, paraphrase around it, or use a bracketed placeholder by standard convention. No quoted words are changed or added.

findings.passage: He also explained the failure on camera within days, which an image-protective Three rarely does.
findings.problem: 'Explains failures on camera' is used as a Seven-over-Three discriminator three times ('Saying it on his own channel is not', this line, and the closing list in 'The case for Type 3'). Yet the article's own setup says a variety streamer's job blurs the motives. For a creator whose format is candid talking to camera, a quick public account of a failure can also be image management. An intelligent newcomer will see the argument skip the caveat it applied to novelty and numbers.
findings.acceptance_test: The article says once that confessional video is part of his job and weights that evidence accordingly. Otherwise it is dropped from the discriminator list in 'The case for Type 3'. Either way the point appears in one place, not three.

protected_passages.passage: He told YouTube no. YouTube fought for him. He then told Twitch he had decided on YouTube, to see what it would say.
protected_passages.reason: Fast, concrete and sourced. Short declaratives turn a contract negotiation into a scene with a twist that a newcomer follows without any background.

protected_passages.passage: Yet the fantasy he describes is not of working harder to be seen. It is of arriving and no longer having to try.
protected_passages.reason: The profile's sharpest original reading. It turns his own Type 3 evidence into something more specific and surprising, and it is grounded in his quoted 'success would fall on my lap'.

protected_passages.passage: "I would stop pursuing the very long boring tiresome road of actually doing that thing because it felt good enough to get a little crumb of what that thing was like."
protected_passages.reason: The most memorable detail in the piece and the clearest window into the motive for a reader with no typology. Keep the quote whole.

protected_passages.passage: Effort is not his problem. Effort without a live stake is.
protected_passages.reason: A precise turn that settles the streak/Evo counterevidence without dodging it. It gives the reader a usable model of the person.

protected_passages.passage: He may be narrating a plateau as a preference; a Three is good at making a ceiling sound like a choice, and this profile cannot rule that out.
protected_passages.reason: Honest, quotable counterargument placed right next to the main evidence. It builds the reader's trust in the type call.

assessment: Orientation is mostly strong. The coin-flip cold open is specific and sourced. By the third paragraph a newcomer knows who he is, and the type section defines Seven and Three in plain words and states the test ('which motive wins when they diverge'). The first three H2s build well: the subathon's two motives, the Twitch exit, then the trophy crumb, the best insight in the piece. Momentum sags in the middle. Four passages each claim to be the decisive evidence and several sections end on 'both fit', so the reader keeps score instead of learning more about Ludwig. The last section mixes record limits, a relationship update and a death-themed coda under one heading. Two context problems would mislead a newcomer: the Valorant/wedding anecdote reverses what he chose, and the drinking 'contradiction' is undone by the rule the article quotes. The hook also sets up 'leaving the bigger number' with a story in which he took the bigger offer. Jargon (Mogul Mail/Money/Moves, Tip To Tip, wings) and a few elided quotes that don't parse are easy fixes. The body runs about 3,800 words, above the 2,000 to 3,500 target, and tightening the seesaw middle would help pacing. Similarity diagnostic: not tripped. The top pair (kareem-rahma, 0.093) shares only a generic 'which motive wins' framing, not an argument or details; no meaningful reuse found. Risk flags: sensitive_allegations (Mang0 harassment and enabling criticism, disclosed family alcoholism, self-described gambling addiction) and contested_typing (medium-confidence 7 against a serious 3, with 6 and an 8 wing raised).
